docs.title: Student Guide: Learning Differential Calculus
docs.text:
Welcome to your interactive guide to mathematical analysis! In this module, we will master the fundamental concept of Limits.

How to use this guide

Interactive Mode Active: Type your answer in the box and click "Check". If you are stuck, click the "Show Solution" tab to see the step-by-step math.

docs.title: 1. Practice Task
docs.text:
Consider the sequence \(a_n = \frac{n+1}{n}\). What is the limit as \(n \to \infty\)?

Your Answer:

Check

Show Solution

Step-by-Step Calculation:

  1. Split the fraction: $\(\frac{n+1}{n} = \frac{n}{n} + \frac{1}{n} = 1 + \frac{1}{n}\)$
  2. As \(n \to \infty\), the term \(\frac{1}{n}\) becomes \(0\).
  3. Result: $\(1 + 0 = 1\)$

docs.title: 2. Practice Task (The "Hole")
docs.text:
Compute the limit of \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 1}{x - 1}\) as \(x \to 1\).

Your Answer:

Check

Show Solution

Analysis:

  1. Direct substitution gives \(\frac{0}{0}\) (Undefined).
  2. Factorize: \(x^2 - 1 = (x-1)(x+1)\).
  3. Simplify: $\(\lim_{x \to 1} \frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{x-1} = \lim_{x \to 1} (x+1)\)$
  4. Solve: \(1 + 1 = 2\).

docs.title: 3. Practice Task (Indeterminate Form)
docs.text:
Compute the limit of \(f(x) = \frac{2x^2 - 2}{x - 1}\) as \(x \to 1\).

Your Answer:

Check

Show Solution
  1. Factor out 2: \(2(x^2 - 1)\).
  2. Expand: \(2(x-1)(x+1)\).
  3. Cancel \((x-1)\).
  4. Limit is \(2(1+1) = 4\).

docs.title: Task A: Sequence Limit
docs.text:
Find limit of \(a_n = \frac{3n}{n+2}\).

Check

Show Solution

Divide by highest power (\(n\)): $\(\frac{3}{1 + \frac{2}{n}} \to \frac{3}{1+0} = 3\)$

docs.title: Task B: Function Limit
docs.text:
Find limit of \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 + 3x}{x}\) as \(x \to 0\).

Check

Show Solution

Factor out \(x\): $\(\frac{x(x+3)}{x} = x+3\)$ As \(x \to 0\), result is \(0+3 = 3\).

Good luck on your journey through analysis!
